stem:
Falguni starts with a full bottle. She pours out $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of the bottle, then pours out $\dfrac{1}{2}$ of what remains.

Which claim correctly tracks the amounts?

options.text: After the first pour, $\dfrac{2}{3}$ remains; $\dfrac{1}{2}$ of that remaining is $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of the bottle, so $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of the bottle is left.
She pours $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of the bottle and then $\dfrac{1}{2}$ of the original bottle, so $\dfrac{5}{6}$ is poured in total.
The second pour of $\dfrac{1}{2}$ of the original rebuilds the remaining $\dfrac{2}{3}$.
The two pour fractions multiply to make the remaining amount, so the bottle ends with $\dfrac{1}{3}\times\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{1}{6}$.

teacher.key_rationale: After removing 1/3, 2/3 remains; half of that remaining is 1/3 of the bottle, leaving 1/3. Applying the second fraction to the original whole, reversing remaining and pour, or multiplying the pour fractions as the leftover all miss the changing whole.
